analysis: The supplied units are head-side excerpts (lines 3700-4194) of historical CHANGELOG.md entries for v0.9.0 to v0.9.9. The patch metadata shows the actual PR change is only at head lines 11-333, which add the v0.10.8 candidate section and are not visible in these units, so I could not examine them. The visible lines are unchanged historical documentation. They hold no executable code, no configuration changes, and no security-control changes, so I found no concrete regression. The excerpts mention App Attest, the prefix cache (T-041, SEC-035), and the add-on or rollout gating. These are descriptions of previously shipped behavior, not new changes. Nothing in the visible text widens the cache TTL, weakens account scoping, changes the HMAC lookup tags, or loosens authorization. The v0.10.8 notes in the patch excerpt concern two-Mac pairing, same-build enforcement, auto-update, and pair approval caps. They are truncated, so the next pass should check whether they have any security effect. The points to check are fail-closed behavior on a build mismatch, the update path's signed-artifact verification (T-034/T-054), and the cap on coordinator pair approvals. The changelog cannot establish any of these behaviors. The code that implements the v0.10.8 pairing and update behavior is not in this batch, so I make no conclusion about it and request deeper review for that portion.
